assessment: Chest infection, possibly early pneumonia on the right side, given the symptoms and physical findings. Patient is allergic to penicillin, so amoxicillin is contraindicated.
objective: On examination, crackles were heard at the right lower lung base. Temperature was 99.4, blood pressure 138/86, and oxygen saturation 96%. Chest X-ray, complete blood count, and HbA1c test were ordered. Patient was prescribed azithromycin 500 mg once daily after food for 5 days, paracetamol 650 mg for fever, and metformin extended release 500 mg once daily with dinner.
plan: Start azithromycin 500 mg once daily after food for 5 days, paracetamol 650 mg for fever, and metformin extended release 500 mg once daily with dinner. Order chest X-ray, complete blood count, and HbA1c test. Advise to rest, avoid sweets, and seek immediate care if breathlessness or fever persists. Patient can return to work after 2 days of rest.
subjective: Patient Mr. Kumar presented with a two-week history of dry cough, occasional yellow phlegm in the morning, and night-time fever. He experiences mild breathlessness on stairs. No chest pain or blood in phlegm. He stopped metformin due to stomach upset, continues amlodipine, and has a family history of diabetes and heart disease. He used to smoke but quit 5 years ago and does not drink alcohol. He has a history of penicillin allergy and his mother had diabetes, his father had a heart attack at 60.
